title: Quantum Fluctuations in Bose--Einstein Condensates:Microscopic Correlations and Moment Bounds
authors: Mauris Chueng, Keheng Zhu, Hexiang Wang
abstract: We study higher moments of quantum fluctuations and microscopic correlation energy in the three-dimensional Gross--Pitaevskii regime. For a smooth, compactly supported, nonnegative radial interaction and an $N$-independent normalized initial condensate wave function in $H^6$, we propagate the third spectral moment of a positive correlated energy along the exact many-body evolution. A uniform initial bound controls the third moment of the depletion number and sixth moments of collective one-particle fluctuations on every compact time interval, independently of $N$. For a nonzero interaction and a smooth, compactly supported initial condensate, we also identify the excitation-energy measure at scale $N^2$, weighted by the first energy. This limit holds for norm-convergent pure-state families with a uniform bound on the initial third correlated-energy moment. Its positive-energy part is a spectral measure of the relative scattering operator $-2Δ+v$, multiplied by a time-dependent dressed contact. We compute the radial density and prove strict positivity of the contact for nonzero references with finite kinetic energy and finite mean excitation number. The same evolving states have bounded physical fluctuation moments and excitation-energy moments of order $p>1$ bounded below by a positive multiple of $N^{2p-2}$, in the extended spectral sense. Inverse powers of the positive initial energy construct admissible pure and mixed families. For the norm-convergent pure-state class, we determine the scaled interaction-energy moments for $1\le p<2$ and bound the second moment by $O(N^2)$. A finite cubic approximation has norm error $O(N^{-3/16})$ on the energy form domain and $O(N^{-5/4})$ on a stronger initial domain of its generator.
summary: This paper provides a rigorous mathematical analysis of quantum fluctuations in Bose-Einstein Condensates operating in the Gross-Pitaevskii regime. It tracks the evolution of higher moments of energy and fluctuations, proving that certain moments remain bounded independently of the particle number N. The results are significant for understanding the quantitative limits of mean-field approximations in interacting quantum gases.
main_problem: The paper investigates the behavior of higher moments of quantum fluctuations and the microscopic correlation energy within the context of the three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii regime.
main_result: It establishes that initial bounds on the third moment of correlated energy control the third moment of depletion and sixth moment of fluctuations independently of particle number N. Furthermore, it identifies the excitation-energy measure at scale N^2 for interacting systems.
method: The analysis employs rigorous mathematical techniques, including propagating spectral moments along the exact many-body evolution in Fock space and deriving detailed error estimates for approximations.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC) governed by a Hamiltonian related to the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, involving a smooth, compactly supported, nonnegative radial interaction potential v.
key_observables: Third spectral moment of correlated energy, third moment of depletion number, sixth moment of collective one-particle fluctuations, and the excitation-energy measure.
important_parameters: The analysis is highly dependent on the particle number N, with results scaling with powers of N (e.g., N^2, N^{2p-2}).
main_assumptions: Assumes the interaction potential v is smooth, compactly supported, nonnegative, and radial, and that the initial state has specific uniform bounds on its correlated energy moment.
paper_structure: The paper follows a highly technical structure, progressing from setting up the Hamiltonian and initial conditions to analyzing correlation transformations, deriving energy estimates, and finally determining the behavior of higher moments and spectral measures.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical rigor to the study of quantum fluctuations in BECs, offering precise bounds and convergence results that are crucial for understanding the transition from mean-field descriptions to fully quantum regimes.
